USS Constellation. A Kitty Hawk-class aircraft carrier commissioned in 1961, serving through the Vietnam War and Cold War as one of America's premier power-projection platforms. Her long career spanned five decades of Cold War operations and demonstrated sustained American naval dominance across multiple theaters.

She was the third ship of the Kitty Hawk-class, optimized for sustained power projection in distant theaters. During the Vietnam War, Constellation conducted multiple combat deployments, launching thousands of air sorties against North Vietnamese targets and providing sustained air support to allied forces. Throughout her career, she participated in Cold War forward presence missions, maintaining American naval supremacy in the Mediterranean and Western Pacific.

Constellation served as a flagship for multiple carrier strike groups, commanding task forces and demonstrating American commitment to regional allies from NATO to Japan. She was distinguished for exceptional crew training programs and material condition maintenance, earning the Naval Efficiency Award multiple times during her operational career. After 42 years of service, she was decommissioned in 2003 and converted to a museum ship in San Diego, where her flight deck now hosts historical exhibits and veteran gatherings. Her four-decade service embodied American naval presence and strategic deterrence throughout the Cold War era, while her air wings had delivered sustained combat power in Southeast Asian operations aboard one of the most capable carrier designs of the entire Cold War period.
